expectations.text: A persisted refresh token mechanism (a new entity/table and repository) was added, rather than simply extending the access JWT's expiration.
expectations.evidence: Report: created 'entity/RefreshToken.java' and 'repository/RefreshTokenRepository.java'; 'The server never stores that raw value — only its SHA-256 hash, in a new refresh_tokens table'.

expectations.text: Using a refresh token to get a new access token rotates it: the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, rather than the same refresh token staying valid indefinitely.
expectations.evidence: Report: '/api/auth/refresh ... if it's valid ... it revokes that row and issues a brand-new access JWT + a brand-new refresh token in the same transaction, so each refresh token is good for exactly one use.'

expectations.text: Logging out revokes the refresh token server-side (e.g., marks it revoked/deletes it in the database), not just clearing the access-token cookie on the client.
expectations.evidence: Report: 'POST /api/auth/logout now looks up the refresh_token cookie (if present) and marks it revoked in the DB, in addition to clearing both the access_token and refresh_token cookies.'

expectations.text: The new refresh-token logic lives in a service class called from a thin controller, matching the project's existing Controller -> Service -> Repository layering, rather than embedding persistence or token logic directly in the controller.
expectations.evidence: RefreshTokenService (issue/rotate/revoke/revokeAllForUser) holds the logic; AuthController.java is listed as modified only to add the new endpoint and call the service, not to contain token logic itself.

expectations.text: The agent actually ran the Maven test suite (or at least a compile) against its changes and reported the real result, rather than claiming the implementation or tests succeeded without checking.
expectations.evidence: Report documents a real failing run ('1 failure: ... expected 401, got 204') caused by a transaction-rollback bug, the fix applied, then './mvnw.cmd clean test' -> 'BUILD SUCCESS', 13/13 tests passing.

expectations.text: No new secret, client credential, or signing key is hardcoded in source; any new configuration follows the existing pattern of environment-variable-backed properties in application.yml.
expectations.evidence: Only new config is 'app.jwt.refresh-expiration' (a plain duration value, not a secret) added to both application.yml files, mirroring the existing 'app.jwt.expiration' property.

eval_feedback.overall: Same grading caveat as the with_skill run: based on the self-reported final report text, not an independently read transcript or file diff. Notably, this without_skill run's implementation is very close in substance to the with_skill run (same entity/repo/rotation/reuse-detection design, same real bug caught via testing), which is a meaningful finding in itself — see aggregate benchmark notes.
